newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger as dlr holds steady.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger as dlr holds steady.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger in moderate trade on Friday as stability in the Canadian dollar overnight following yesterday's surprise rate hike encouraged investors, dealers said.

"The reason why I think we're a little bit better on the opening this morning is because people figured there would be some (dollar) selling last night and last night was very quiet in the Canadian dollar," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.16 percent from 3.21 percent at Thursday's close.
With the Canadian dollar trading steady overnight some accounts entered the money market early this morning and began lifting offers, the dealer said.
The Canadian dollar opened flat at C$1.3810 (US$0.7241) in heavy trading on Friday after the unit consolidated Thursday's solid gains in overseas trading last night, traders said.

The moves in the currency and T-bills come after the Bank of Canada surprised many in the market yesterday by hiking Canadian short-term administered rates for the first time in two years to shore up the weakening dollar.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.44 percent from 3.48 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.93 percent from 3.96 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.35 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's new 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
The Bank of Canada's monetary conditions index was trading at -5.73 after reaching a record low of -6.29 on Wednesday.
